items.title: Mason council meets as $1B data center seeks city utilities via annexation
items.dek: A proposed facility in Vevay Township seeks Mason city utilities via annexation or 425 agreement. The 8/17 council meeting occurs after the city voted on data-center zoning three times in six months and adopted noise rules in June.
items.findings: Proposed Mason-area project: undisclosed developer, $1B pledged investment, seeking city utilities via annexation/425 agreement | Vevay Twp. site spans ~400 acres at Columbia/College Rds. | 12/15/2025: 4-3 vote for 90-day data center zoning moratorium | 2/2/2026: 5-2 vote adopting Ordinance 266 (M-3 Technology Innovation District) | 3/16/2026: 4-2 vote repealing Ordinance 266 | 6/15/2026: adopted Ordinance 272 (noise/vibration standards) | No specific data-center item or packet details extractable for 8/17 meeting (agenda page only lists date and packet link)
items.perspective: Mason City Council has reversed course on data-center zoning multiple times since late 2025. Tonight offers public comment on the regular agenda with no confirmed vote or reading scheduled on the project; any annexation decision would tie directly to utility access.

items.title: Caledonia mulls data center moratorium extension amid 68th-Kraft inquiries
items.dek: Caledonia Township Planning Commission meets tonight to address its standing ban on new data center proposals. Developer interest has surfaced for land at 68th Street and Kraft Avenue, though no formal applications can advance under the current rules.
items.findings: Moratorium blocks data center applications | Inquiries noted for 68th Street and Kraft Avenue parcels | Agenda packet contents not extractable from township site
items.perspective: The commission has not approved any data center projects since the moratorium began. Tonight's discussion is expected to cover extension or ordinance drafting; any changes would require public comment and subsequent board action. The outcome ties directly to regional patterns of large-acreage proposals facing farmland, water and tax-base questions in nearby townships.

items.title: Coldwater schedules joint meeting on data center zoning rules
items.dek: City officials say no proposals are active, but social media rumors have sparked concern over future facilities. The joint meeting with the Planning Commission and CBPU Board will hear from an MSU Extension zoning expert Monday at 5:30 p.m.
items.source: City of Coldwater, Planning Commission and CBPU Board agenda
items.findings: No active data center proposals exist in Coldwater per city officials | Meeting scheduled for Monday at 5:30 p.m. at Henry L. Brown Municipal Building | MSU Extension expert specializing in land-use and zoning will present | Michigan Zoning Enabling Act prevents outright bans on data centers | Planning Commission previously rejected a temporary freeze | City focusing on drafting strict permanent ordinances to dictate operational boundaries and preserve municipal resources | Meeting described as foundational step for gathering community feedback before final ordinances are drafted and adopted
items.perspective: City Manager Keith Baker says the focus is on drafting strict permanent ordinances because state law prevents outright bans. The Planning Commission rejected a temporary freeze, noting that a definitive legal framework would protect neighborhoods from noise and utility strain without stalling broader economic growth. items.title: Kalamazoo weighs data center moratorium over health and safety risks
items.dek: The City Commission is set to consider a resolution pausing new data center projects while staff examines public health, safety, and environmental impacts. No formal data center proposal is before the city, though a cannabis facility owner floated redevelopment of its site earlier this year. Residents 30 minutes away have reason to watch as neighboring townships already enacted similar pauses amid farmland and infrastructure concerns.
items.findings: Per recent commission discussion, staff will draft a resolution addressing data centers’ public health, safety, and welfare concerns for the Aug. 17 vote | The packet and agenda details remain unavailable as of Aug. 16, with no specific parcels, acreage, megawatts, or abatement terms disclosed | Background coverage shows no formal data center application or approval for the Harbor Farmz site at 2839 Full Circle Drive | Public opposition to a data center concept was raised at the June 15, 2026 commission meeting | Oshtemo, Pavilion, and Texas townships plus Portage have enacted temporary data center moratoriums while reviewing zoning
items.perspective: The Kalamazoo City Commission has not previously voted on data center projects; a June 2026 statement from officials confirmed no proposal had been submitted or approved for the Harbor Farmz cannabis facility. The Aug. 17 regular business meeting follows a Committee of the Whole session and will consider the resolution, with any zoning moratorium process to begin later at the Planning Commission.
